bill.title: To direct the Federal Trade Commission to conduct an investigation and submit to Congress a report on unfair or deceptive acts or practices that may be prevalent in the advertising or marketing of preterm infant formula and to issue regulations to prohibit unfair or deceptive acts or practices related to the advertising or marketing of preterm infant formula, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require the Federal Trade Commission to investigate whether companies use unfair or deceptive practices when advertising or marketing formula designed for premature infants. Based on that investigation, the FTC would report its findings to Congress and issue regulations to prohibit such practices.

industries.rationale: Preterm infant formula manufacturers would face new FTC investigation and potential advertising and marketing regulations.
Retailers selling preterm infant formula may be affected by new marketing and advertising restrictions.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
